result.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
result.summary: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out? The paradigm is considered advantageous because the reasoning is native to the visual medium, unfolding directly in the frames rather than through language or code. Whether this native route is in fact the more reliable path to visual reasoning has not been tested against a symbolic alternative under the same conditions. We therefore pose the same tasks, with identical inputs, output specification and evaluator, to both media: rather than denoising pixels, a coding agent writes a program that renders the answer video, which an unmodified rule-based evaluator scores. On VBVR-Pro-Bench (Xu et al., 2026), a 500-instance suite spanning five cognitive categories with symbolic ground truth, the agent receives the same first frame and prompt as the video model, with no access to ground truth, metadata or generation models, and one attempt per instance. Three closed-model agents (Codex with gpt-6-astra, Claude Code with Fable 5.1 and Gemini CLI with Gemini 3.1 Pro) score 0.923, 0.894 and 0.893, each more than 0.22 above the strongest video model. Among 23 runnable open-weight models, the best, GLM-5, reaches 0.572, above all video models except the RL-trained one. Together, we show that for tasks whose solutions can be computed from a first frame and a prompt, program synthesis is currently a substantially more reliable route to visual reasoning than video generation. We further distinguish depictive programs, which navigate the image to recover a transferable scheme, from propositional programs, which operate on hard-coded values, revealing how visual reasoning unfolds in agent-written programs and what it implies for its nature of reasoning in general.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 VBVR-Pro-Bench 上用相同首帧、提示与评测器，对比视频生成模型与 coding agent 编写渲染程序两条路线，发现三个闭源 agent 得分均高出最强视频模型 0.22 以上，并区分「描绘式」与「命题式」程序以刻画视觉推理如何在代码中展开。
AI.relevance_reason: 它直接质疑「推理在与视觉同质的媒介中更可靠」这一前提，对 LVR 以视觉 latent 承载推理的动机构成外部对照；其描绘式/命题式的区分可能对应 latent 状态是否保留并真正使用视觉细节的问题，可供核查。
